 Asian Paints Dividend 2026: 575% cash payout announced with Q2FY27 results — Check record date
 Written By Anubhav Maurya Published: 2:23 PM, Oct 29, 2026 | Updated: 2:23 PM, Oct 29, 2026 Asian Paints on Thursday reported a 7.5 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit. The results were below Zee Business estimates on key parameters, including revenue, EBITDA and profit after tax (PAT). Asian Paints on Thursday reported a 7.5 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit. Image Credit: Canva Asian Paints on Thursday reported a 7.5 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit after minority interest to Rs 1,067.6 crore for the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2 FY27), compared with Rs 993.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
 The company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 9,976.51 crore from Rs 8,531.27 crore in the year-ago period. Consolidated net sales rose 16.9 per cent to Rs 9,953.9 crore from Rs 8,513.7 crore a year earlier.
 Asian Paints Zee Business estimates 
 The results were below Zee Business estimates on key parameters, including revenue, EBITDA and profit after tax (PAT).
 Zee Business had estimated consolidated revenue at Rs 9,662 crore, EBITDA at Rs 1,643 crore, an EBITDA margin of 17 per cent and PAT at Rs 1,115 crore for the quarter.
 Asian Paints' reported consolidated net sales exceeded the revenue estimate by Rs 291.9 crore. However, its profit after minority interest fell short of the estimated PAT by Rs 47.4 crore. The company's profitability was affected by a decline in its operating margin.
 The company's revenue from operations exceeded Zee Business estimates by Rs 314.51 crore. However, its PBDIT of Rs 1,557.1 crore was Rs 85.9 crore below the estimated EBITDA of Rs 1,643 crore.
 The reported PBDIT margin stood at 15.6 per cent, compared with the estimated margin of 17 per cent. PAT after minority interest was also below estimates, although it increased from the year-ago period.
 Asian Paints Dividend 2026 
 Asian Paints announced an interim dividend of Rs 5.75 per equity share (575 per cent) with a face value of Re 1 each for the financial year ending March 31, 2027.
 Asian Paints Dividend Record Date 
 The company fixed November 4, 2026, as the record date for the interim dividend. The dividend will be paid to shareholders on or after November 13, 2026.
 Revenue grows 16.9%, operating margin declines 
 Asian Paints' consolidated net sales increased 16.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 9,953.9 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 8,513.7 crore in Q2 FY26.
 However, the growth in operating profit was slower than the increase in sales. PBDIT rose 3.6 per cent to Rs 1,557.1 crore from Rs 1,503.4 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
 The PBDIT margin declined to 15.6 per cent from 17.7 per cent a year earlier, a contraction of 202 basis points. Profit before tax increased 6.2 per cent to Rs 1,477.8 crore from Rs 1,391.5 crore in the year-ago quarter. Net profit after minority interest rose 7.5 per cent to Rs 1,067.6 crore from Rs 993.6 crore.
 The PAT margin stood at 10.7 per cent, down 94 basis points from the corresponding quarter last year. The figures show that while the company recorded double-digit sales growth, operating profit and net profit grew at a slower pace.
 Decorative business records double-digit value growth 
 Asian Paints' decorative business in India reported volume growth of 6.4 per cent and value growth of 14.5 per cent during the quarter.
 The domestic coatings business recorded value growth of 16.4 per cent, with industrial coatings continuing to contribute to the business's growth.
 The company said it was implementing another round of staggered price increases in its decorative business to counter sustained raw material inflation.
 The pricing measures come as the company seeks to address input cost pressures while maintaining growth in its domestic business.
 Asian Paints also commissioned Phase 1 of its vinyl acetate ethylene (VAE) plant at Dahej during the quarter. The company said the facility would pave the way for a new wave of innovation.
 International business grows 29.5%, profit declines 
 Asian Paints' international business recorded a 29.5 per cent year-on-year increase in net sales to Rs 1,095.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 846 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
 In constant currency terms, sales increased 23.7 per cent, with the company reporting growth across all regions.
 However, profit before tax from the international business declined 31 per cent during the quarter to Rs 52.7 crore.
 For the first half of FY27, international business net sales increased 28.4 per cent to Rs 2,032.1 crore from Rs 1,582.1 crore in the corresponding period last year.
 Profit before tax for the first half rose to Rs 126.8 crore from Rs 114.4 crore a year earlier.
 The company's industrial businesses also reported higher sales.
 Net sales of Asian Paints PPG, or APPPG, increased 28 per cent to Rs 374.5 crore from Rs 292.6 crore. However, profit before tax declined to Rs 17.2 crore from Rs 25.9 crore.
 For PPG Asian Paints, or PPGAP, net sales rose 33.7 per cent to Rs 794.8 crore from Rs 594.3 crore. Profit before tax increased to Rs 112.9 crore from Rs 102.8 crore.
 Home décor businesses report mixed performance 
 Asian Paints' home décor businesses reported mixed results during the quarter. The bath fittings business recorded an 18.5 per cent increase in net sales to Rs 94 crore from Rs 79.3 crore in the year-ago quarter. It reported a profit before tax of Rs 8.7 crore, compared with a loss before tax of Rs 4 crore a year earlier.
 The kitchen business reported a 13 per cent increase in net sales to Rs 110.3 crore from Rs 97.7 crore. However, its loss before tax widened to Rs 7.9 crore from Rs 3.6 crore.
 Net sales of White Teak declined 11.8 per cent to Rs 23.3 crore, while Weatherseal's sales fell 1.8 per cent to Rs 20.3 crore during the quarter.
